title: Micron or Nvidia: If I Could Only Buy and Hold One of These Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stocks for the Next 5 Years, It Would Be This One - The Motley Fool
content: Micron and Nvidia both have compelling tailwinds as investments in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure accelerate. The artificial intelligence (AI) revolution has created a generational opportunity for semiconductor companies. As AI hyperscalers like Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms continue investing in data centers, demand for advanced processors, memory chips, and networking equipment is accelerating. Two companies are benefiting enormously from this trend: Nvidia (NVDA -9.26%) and Micron Technology (MU -17.46%). Nvidia dominates the market for graphics processing units (GPUs), while Micron supplies the memory required to power accelerated computing systems. While both companies are experiencing remarkable growth, their long-term investment theses are fundamentally different. Micron is capitalizing on an unprecedented shortage of high bandwidth memory (HBM), while Nvidia is quietly transforming into a diversified AI infrastructure and software company. If I could buy only one of these stocks and hold it through 2030, my choice would be Nvidia. Here's why. Micron's HBM products are essential components for AI accelerators, allowing GPU clusters to process enormous amounts of data quickly and efficiently. As Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, and other semiconductor companies design more powerful chips, demand for HBM will continue to surge. Meanwhile, Micron's DRAM and NAND memory businesses are benefiting from growing demand across data centers, smartphones, computers, and enterprise storage systems. During its fiscal fourth quarter of 2026 (ended Sept. 3), Micron generated $54.2 billion in revenue, compared with just $11.3 billion in the same period last year. Net income reached $37.7 billion, while operating cash flow climbed to nearly $44 billion. For the full fiscal year, Micron's revenue increased to approximately $133.2 billion, up 256% year over year. Somebody is going to make a fortune on Anthropic’s IPO. It probably won’t be regular investors waiting for the day it goes public. Unless investors know where to look. Because two companies anyone can buy today already own pieces of Anthropic. And one of them owns a piece of OpenAI, too. These figures underscore how dramatically AI is changing the memory market. Importantly, Micron is also expanding production of its HBM4 and HBM4E products, which are designed to support more demanding workloads across agentic AI, robotics, autonomous systems, and other next-generation applications. Even so, there is a potential problem with Micron's investment thesis. The memory industry is historically cyclical. When demand exceeds available supply, prices rise, allowing manufacturers to generate unusually high profits. In turn, manufacturers invest aggressively in additional production capacity. Eventually, that new capacity catches up with demand, causing prices and profit margins to normalize. By 2030, Micron could be a substantially larger company while also facing more competition, greater production capacity, and less favorable pricing. This is why I think the company's growth trajectory warrants some caution. Nvidia's investment thesis is considerably broader than Micron's. During its fiscal second quarter (ended July 26), the company generated $96.2 billion in revenue -- representing 106% year-over-year growth. Its data center business accounted for approximately $89 billion, reflecting ongoing demand for AI compute. However, focusing solely on Nvidia's GPUs misses how the company is expanding. Consider its partnership with Marvell Technology (MRVL -16.43%). In March, Nvidia announced a $2 billion investment in Marvell as part of a strategic collaboration involving custom AI processors, networking technology, and silicon photonics. Through its NVLink Fusion platform, AI developers can integrate specialized chips with Nvidia's broader computing architecture, including CPUs, networking equipment, and rack-scale infrastructure. This is important because the hyperscalers are developing their own custom processors rather than relying exclusively on general-purpose GPUs. Instead of treating that trend as a competitive threat, Nvidia is positioning itself to participate in the custom-chip ecosystem. The company is also expanding into telecommunications. Nvidia's $1 billion strategic investment in Nokia (NOK -9.69%) supports the development of AI-powered radio access networks, commonly called AI-RAN. These systems aim to transform traditional telecommunications infrastructure into distributed platforms that support AI applications on edge devices. Nvidia's ambitions extend beyond hardware. Its CUDA software ecosystem is a major competitive advantage, while platforms such as the Nemotron open AI models are expanding its presence in areas traditionally dominated by frontier model developers like Anthropic and Google DeepMind. All this means that Nvidia is no longer just selling processors that power AI. The company is increasingly supplying the networking, software, infrastructure, and models that make AI useful. To me, Nvidia is a more diversified investment opportunity relative to Micron. Micron's profitability remains heavily influenced by the current supply-and-demand imbalance in the memory market. Sure, Nvidia faces competition and cyclical risks, too. But its growing portfolio of software, networking, custom chips, telecommunications, and open-source models provides several opportunities to generate revenue outside of the core GPU franchise. On a deeper level, these businesses reinforce one another. A customer deploying Nvidia's GPUs is likely to also purchase its networking equipment, adopt its software tools, and eventually build applications using its AI models. That creates an integrated ecosystem that competitors will struggle to replicate at scale. While Micron can still deliver impressive upside as long as the memory shortage persists, Nvidia doesn't need a single semiconductor market to remain supply-constrained to succeed in the long run. The artificial intelligence (AI) trade has whipsawed this year, and so has its flagbearer Nvidia (NVDA). The chip-designing giant hit its record highs last month and has since lost 15% from those levels. As of last week's closing prices, the stock's year-to-date returns trail both the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index ($IUXX) and the diversified S&P 500 Index ($SPX). Nvidia's performance would seem at odds with its financial results, though. For instance, its revenues more than doubled in the most recent reported quarter, and its guidance for fiscal Q3 implies they will nearly double again. For the next fiscal year, Nvidia guided a 70% revenue growth, which is astonishing considering the high base. Moreover, at a time when companies are hard-pressed even to guide for the next quarter, Nvidia went out of its way to provide a forecast for the next fiscal year. Micron vs. SanDisk: China's DRAM Scare Hit Both Stocks, but 1 Is the Better Buy Ford and GM Are Taking Different Roads, but 1 Stock Races Ahead Nvidia Stock Looks Surprisingly Cheap. Why NVDA Could Rise 61%. Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today! Following Nvidia's fiscal Q2 earnings release in August, I noted that despite the strong growth and reasonable valuations, Nvidia wasn't a "buy." With NVDA coming off those levels, let's explore the stock's outlook. The recent weakness in NVDA could be attributed to the weakness in the AI trade. Incidentally, all the Magnificent 7 names, which happen to be Nvidia's biggest customer set, plunged following their September quarter earnings, in part due to growing anxiety over their AI capex. Since much of this capex lands in Nvidia's coffers, the stock too fell alongside. To make things worse, Intel's (INTC) tepid Q4 guidance led to a sell-off in other chip stocks, which also put pressure on NVDA. On a broader level, there are concerns over the sustainability of Nvidia's growth since customers like Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL) and Amazon (AMZN) are working on their own chips. They are not only using them internally but also aggressively scouting third-party customers. Selling chips to third parties would help hyperscalers justify their burgeoning AI capex and offset some of their cash burn. Then there are fears over "circular financing" and off-balance-sheet financing. So, we have Nvidia investing in companies that buy its chips, while cloud companies like Amazon, Microsoft (MSFT), and Alphabet — the three biggest players in that order — are investing in AI startups that have developed into their biggest cloud customers, driving much of the incremental growth. While Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is dismissive of the very term circular financing and, during the Q2 call, said that he regrets not investing in these companies early, terming it an "once-in-a-generation opportunity," at least a section of the market is getting apprehensive over such transactions. Off-balance-sheet financing is another concern, and Nvidia has been providing credit guarantees for its customers' data centers. There are reports that Nvidia is in talks to provide credit guarantees to Nscale for a data center that Anthropic would use. Such deals add a layer of risk for Nvidia investors and would be catastrophic if AI actually turns out to be a bubble and goes bust. That, however, is not my base case assumption, and while there are visible signs of exuberance in AI, the technology holds a lot of promise. I believe the sell-off in NVDA stock has gone a bit too far and see the recent pullback as a buying opportunity, particularly as the company heads into its Q3 earnings call. While Nvidia's recent quarterly earnings have been followed by a decline in its stock price despite the company delivering a "beat and raise" quarter, the setup looks nice to me ahead of the Q3 report. At around the $200 price level, Nvidia is offering an attractive entry point with a price-to-earnings multiple of around 23x. While Nvidia has had a dismal run this year, I believe the stock should make up for it in the final two months of the year, and I see it ending the year higher than these levels. title: How Are Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq Futures Trading After Blue Wave Rally? - Stocktwits
content: U.S. stock futures were mixed overnight late Wednesday as markets awaited the final results of the November midterms even as the Democrats swept both chambers of Congress. As of 09:30 p.m. EST, Dow futures gained 0.24%, while the S&P 500 futures were down 0.04% and Nasdaq-100 futures fell 0.46%. On Wednesday, all three U.S. benchmark indexes rallied on the blue tidal wave. The Dow Jones Industrial Average led the climb, adding more than 1,500 points to close 3% higher. The S&P 500 gained 1.58% at close, while the Nasdaq Composite closed up 1.44%. Markets welcomed a Democratic victory in early voting counts on Wednesday, sending stocks higher on anticipation of a potential end to the Iran war and expectations of an improvement in economic policy as well as an end to Trump’s tariffs. The Nov. 3 U.S. midterm election results flipped control in both chambers of Congress, with Democrats in the lead. While final results are still being counted, Democrats flipped at least seven Senate seats, 24 House districts, five governorships, and twelve state legislative chambers, securing an early reported majority of at least 231–141 in the House and 54–44 in the Senate. Key red states including Texas, Iowa, Ohio, Maine, and Kansas also flipped blue, making history. Consumer discretionary names such as Walmart gained following the initial counting. However, AI-lined and data center build-out names trended lower as markets expect a pullback in support to the industry amid Democratic leadership. Yorkville Advisors partner and managing director Dan Ives said in a post on X, “Democratic blue tidal wave across the Senate and House was a seismic shift that will have a negative impact on the pace of the AI Revolution buildout in the US over the next few years. Will slow the pace of the planned 800 to 1,000 datacenters across the US fueling the AI Revolution…some investors will like the “slower pace”…others view it as adding risk. We estimate 10% of datacenters will not happen now.” However, Fundstrat’s Tom Lee took an opposing stance, saying in an interview with CNBC on Wednesday that Democratic gains in the midterms could prove positive for stocks and lead to a 15-20% rally in tech stocks, calling Wednesday’s tech selloff a “knee-jerk reaction.” Oil prices declined sharply as expectations over the end of the Iran war rose. Brent crude futures were trading at $93.91 a barrel, down about 0.75%, while WTI crude futures traded 1% lower at $87.24 per barrel. Markets will now be watching for weekly jobless claims data and October’s nonfarm payrolls report later this week. On the earnings front, Toyota Motor Corporation, ConocoPhillips, Sony Group, Airbnb, and Cloudflare are among the top companies reporting their quarterly results on Thursday. Nvidia Corp. (NVDA): The AI darling was on top of the retail radar after a 3% decline in shares as investors were concerned about tighter AI data center rules and delays in AI buildouts amid a Democratic win. Micron Technology Inc. (MU): The chipmaker’s stock plunged 7% at close on Wednesday and continued to decline overnight amid growing concerns for AI-linked names following the early midterm election results. Sandisk Corp. (SNDK): The memory stock plunged nearly 8% at close on Wednesday and dipped further overnight amid similar concerns for tightened AI policy following a blue tidal wave. Nebius Group N.V. (NBIS): The election results also weighed on shares of this AI infrastructure company, with the stock dropping more than 6% at close and down by nearly 3% overnight. IREN Ltd. (IREN): The company garnered attention after The Information reported on Wednesday that Microsoft's lower-than-expected AI data center spending was partially caused by the delays from the Australian cloud computing infrastructure provider. Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) and the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) were down at the time of writing, while the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged higher. Meanwhile, long-term Treasury yields eased late Wednesday, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield trading at 4.853%, while the 30-year yield was at 5.243%. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was up 0.48% amid ‘bearish’ sentiment. Asian markets opened mixed on Thursday. South Korea's KOSPI and Japan’s Nikkei 225 were trading lower at the time of writing. Meanwhile, China’s SSE Composite and Australian stocks edged higher at the open. Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) rose 0.4% overnight late Wednesday as Citigroup disclosed a nearly 64% cut in its stake, while retail bulls argued that SLS009 alone could be worth more than the company. SLS stock rose 3% on Wednesday to $9.14, with shares still down nearly 6% for the week. Citigroup cut its Sellas holding by nearly two-thirds in the third quarter, reducing its position by 207,555 shares, or 64%, to 119,036 shares as of Sept.30, according to Fiscal.ai data on Wednesday’s disclosures. The remaining stake was worth about $1.47 million at quarter-end. Meanwhile, Prospera Financial Services added 12,600 shares, increasing its holding by nearly 70% to 30,719. Eversource Wealth Advisors trimmed its position by roughly 42% to 5,785 shares, while Nemes Rush Group kept its holding unchanged at 10,000 shares. The developments come as Sellas shared Phase 2 results for SLS009, also called Tambiciclib, ahead of a Dec.14 presentation at the American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. The study tested SLS009 with Azacitidine and Venetoclax in 62 previously treated AML patients whose leukemia had returned or stopped responding to venetoclax-based treatment. Across doses, 34% of the 59 patients assessed responded. At the selected dose, 54% of patients with monocytic AML responded, with median survival of 5.8 months. For TP53-mutated AML, the response rate was 57% and median survival was 8.8 months. Sellas reported limited added toxicity and cited historical survival of about 2.5 months in these high-risk groups. Without a concurrent comparison group, however, the figures do not prove a survival benefit. The company is also exploring SLS009 beyond leukemia. In September, it reported activity in laboratory models of pancreatic cancer, although those early findings have yet to establish benefit in patients. CEO Angelos Stergiou highlighted the SLS009 findings in a recent LinkedIn post, while drawing attention to two upcoming data announcements. “These are some of the hardest-to-treat patients in hematology. Seeing this level of activity is exactly why we do this work,” he said. Sellas expects initial results this quarter from its ongoing 80-patient Phase 2 study of SLS009 in newly diagnosed AML. This readout is separate from the completed study being presented at ASH. Stergiou also reiterated that results from the Phase 3 Regal trial of Galinpepimut-S (GPS) are expected soon. Regal reached its prespecified 80th patient death on Oct. 28, triggering the process of locking the database, unblinding treatment assignments and analyzing the final results. The randomized trial is testing whether GPS maintenance treatment helps AML patients live longer after achieving a second complete remission. Preliminary results are expected this quarter. One user said, “009 is not valued for a penny in the market cap.” They added that the asset alone should be worth five times Sellas’ valuation. Another user put SLS009’s standalone value above $5 billion. A separate user said that successful SLS009 frontline results could support a buyout even if GPS disappointed. “Two platforms on goal on multiple indications! I like the odds!” the user said. Another user urged investors to look beyond a single leukemia indication, saying, “The platform valuation is the true forest. AML revenue is just the initial tree.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Redwire Corp. (RDW) stock fell overnight after the space and defense technology company’s third-quarter (Q3) revenue missed Street estimates. However, retail investors appeared unfazed, viewing the dip as a buying opportunity amid record backlog, gross margins and optimism about 2027 growth. Redwire stock traded over 2% lower overnight Wednesday, after tumbling nearly 5% in the regular session. Redwire ended Q3 with $619.7 million in backlog, up nearly 75% from last year. Its book-to-bill ratio reached 1.73 for the quarter, indicating that new contract awards exceeded recognized revenue. The company secured $188.7 million in awards during the period, lifting its trailing 12-month book-to-bill ratio to 1.63. Q3 revenue increased 5.4% to $109 million, missing the analysts’ consensus estimate of $126.5 million, according to Fiscal.ai data. Gross profit more than doubled to $35.2 million, while the net loss narrowed to $23.2 million from $41.2 million in the corresponding period last year. Gross margin expanded to a record 32.3% from 16.3%. Loss per share also narrowed to $0.09 from $0.29 and was above the $0.1 loss estimate. “Although revenue timing continues to be uneven, with another quarter of record gross margins expanding from 16.3% to 32.3% year-over-year, the quality of our revenue is improving as we deliver mission-critical products and solutions across multiple domains,” said CEO Peter Cannito. During the quarter, the company received a $20 million award from the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) to conduct further development and testing of its SabreSat spacecraft for a planned very low-Earth orbit demonstration. Redwire also secured another contract from Axiom Space to manufacture two Roll-Out Solar Array wings for a future space station module. Its defense business also received additional orders for the Stalker platform, including purchases from the U.S. National Guard. Redwire maintained its full-year 2026 revenue outlook of $450 million to $500 million. The company ended September with $538.9 million in total liquidity, a 313.9% jump from the end of 2025. (SPCX) slid over 2% overnight late Wednesday as Goldman Sachs and Apollo Global Management reportedly sought buyers for portions of its $40 billion chip financing, while Democrats’ election victory fueled warnings of greater scrutiny of Elon Musk and his businesses. SPCX stock fell nearly 4% on Wednesday to $135.92, with shares still tracking nearly a 1% gain so far this week. Investors are being offered slices of SpaceX’s $40 billion chip financing worth up to $500 million ahead of the formal sale process, as concerns over AI spending and potential political scrutiny cloud the sector’s outlook, Bloomberg noted. The package, announced in October, secured investor commitments before pricing was finalized, leaving lenders exposed to market swings as they seek buyers. It reportedly includes an $8.3 billion senior-secured loan for banks and several bond tranches for asset managers. Together with a $7 billion lease prepayment, the financing would cover about $47.3 billion of Nvidia equipment, including its next-generation Rubin chips. SpaceX signed a binding commitment in October for an Apollo-managed entity to buy computing equipment and lease it to the company. The agreement is expected to be finalized before year-end, with deliveries and leases beginning in the first half of 2027. Each equipment batch would carry a lease lasting roughly five to five-and-a-quarter years. SpaceX expects to pay about $40 billion in principal, plus interest and other expenses. Called as the largest committed GPU financing, the deal would expand computing capacity for Grok and cloud customers. Several major investment firms have also committed funding. The chips would reportedly be owned by a separate financing vehicle that issues the debt, helping protect SpaceX’s corporate credit ratings. SpaceX would still have to pay rent if the equipment is damaged or unforeseen events disrupt operations. “Rent is owed regardless of equipment condition, casualty or force majeure, providing investors with a clean look-through to SpaceX credit,” an investor presentation reportedly stated. The financing push comes as Republicans warn that Democratic control of Congress could bring greater scrutiny of Musk and other business leaders who worked with President Donald Trump. U.S. Sen.Ted Cruz, a Republican from Texas, warned during the All-In podcast’s election-night coverage that Musk could face congressional subpoenas. “I will say also, look, the Democrats have already foreshadowed that if they have one or both houses, they're going to use subpoenas to go after business executives who've worked with the president, to go after Elon Musk,” Cruz said. “They've already declared they intend to engage in lawfare and in open attacks,” he added. Cruz also warned of growing opposition to AI and data centers, saying that slowing construction could damage the economy. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, a Republican, separately warned that Texas’ incoming Democratic attorney general could target Musk, raising concerns over Tesla’s Gigafactory near Austin. “They’re going to go after Elon Musk. I guarantee you they will do that,” DeSantis said at a Wednesday press conference. He warned that political hostility could complicate Musk’s business operations in Texas. Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson, a Democratic state senator, defeated Republican state Sen.Mayes Middleton to become the first Democrat elected to the office since 1994. Shares of Joby Aviation rose roughly 7% in after-hours trading on Wednesday after the electric air-taxi developer reported third-quarter revenue that topped expectations and raised its full-year outlook while detailing further progress in achieving Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) type certification for its S4 eVTOL. Joby posted $55 million in revenue for the quarter, primarily from its Blade passenger transportation business, which carried more than 44,000 passengers. That figure exceeded analyst estimates of $39.21 million, according to data from Fiscal AI. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook by 15% to a range of $135 million to $140 million. Cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments stood at $2.2 billion as of Sept. 30, including roughly $128 million in net proceeds from an at-the-market equity program during the quarter. Net loss in the quarter narrowed to $211.8 million from $401.2 million a year earlier. Joby expects second-half cash use of $385 million to $415 million. Founder and CEO JoeBen Bevirt said the company made “important progress on the fifth and final stage of certification, completing a wide range of ‘for credit’ testing with the FAA.” Stages one through three of the five-stage process for S4 certification are complete. As of Oct. 30, the company said that it has completed 83% of its efforts at stage 4 completion, while the FAA has done 78%. The company has also begun efforts towards stage 5, it noted. Bevirt added that manufacturing output increased, with 17 aircraft now in production and work orders released to begin the 18th from the Marina line. Output across eight core manufacturing shops rose 37% from the first to the third quarter, while the proportion of articles with recorded nonconformance fell 38%. Toyota production engineers continue to work alongside Joby teams in California. Joby’s J208 aircraft completed what the company described as the first fully autonomous flight of a civilian aircraft across the United States in the quarter. Autonomy-focused contracts with the U.S. Air Force expanded to nearly $37 million, up from nearly $20 million, with the contract ceiling for operational testing raised from $5 million to $50 million, the company said. The company’s plans to acquire defense tech firm Resonant Sciences are progressing, with a deal closing expected in early 2027 and intended to create a dedicated defense business. Fundstrat’s Tom Lee said on Wednesday that Democratic gains in the midterms could ultimately prove positive for stocks rather than a headwind, and voiced optimism for a 15-20% rally in tech stocks. Lee’s optimism for the tech sector stood in contrast to recent comments from Dan Ives of Yorkville Advisors, who anticipated a 10% to 12% correction in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) amid pressure on the tech trade following a Democratic sweep. “It's at least 15%, you know, tech could rally 20%,” Lee said in an interview with CNBC. He added that the sell-off seen on Wednesday was a “knee-jerk reaction because people have to find something to sell to buy what they want to own.” His comments came as the neocloud names like Coreweave (CRWV), Iren (IREN) and others extended their decline and closed down 10-11%. However, big tech names like Apple (AAPL) and Microsoft (MSFT) hit fresh record highs. The Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT), which tracks the overall technology sector, clocked a modest gain of 0.2%. Lee, who is also the chairman of Bitmine Immersion Technologies (BMNR), said that the midterm election outcome is likely to force greater negotiation in Washington, reduce pressure on the Federal Reserve, and leave the central bank freer to operate without concerns over politically driven rate moves. He dismissed the sharp selloff in data-center and AI-related names as a short-term reaction. He maintained that the AI trade remains intact, pointing to rising compute demand as more users adopt AI tools and noting that many states will still welcome the investment, even if on stricter local terms. Lee also pushed back on suggestions that data-center opposition will permanently constrain the sector, arguing that states facing budget needs will have difficulty replacing the revenue these projects generate. “I do think it’s an overreaction today,” he said. However, Ives’ concerns centered around investors giving AI spenders less time to show returns. According to him, some companies may need to limit borrowing and data-center expansion, with Oracle (ORCL) cited as a potential example. Ives, however, remains constructive on select names such as Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL). Ives also expects the Democratic win to result in a ‘seismic shift’ for the AI buildout. Lee said a large share of hedge-fund positioning is still concentrated in technology and that funds are unlikely to rotate heavily into defensive consumer staples. He suggested that investors may rebuild equity exposure into year-end and forecast that technology could rally at least 15%, with upside toward 20% in a move similar to the rebound that followed the Situational Awareness selloff in July. Outside technology, he pointed to financials and industrials as beneficiaries of calmer rate expectations and open capital markets. On the Federal Reserve, Lee noted that odds of a December hike are declining and that falling energy prices could give policymakers more room to pause. Earlier on Wednesday, Lee also said that the technology stocks hit hardest heading into the midterm elections, including memory, semiconductor, and neocloud stocks, are likely to rebound the most. “The Democratic Party and the Republican Party aren’t either enemies or friends of tech. Tech has done well under both administrations,” he said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) fell from ‘neutral’ to ‘bearish’ territory over the past 24 hours, while retail chatter stayed at ‘high’ levels. Meanwhile, sentiment around the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) jumped from ‘bullish’ to ‘extremely bullish’ territory, coupled with ‘high’ message volume. title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Falls 1.3% as Chip Stocks Slide (Nov 2) - Gotrade
content: Gotrade News - In the latest Nvidia stock news, shares of Nvidia (NVDA) fell 1.26% to close at $202.06 on Monday, November 2, 2026. Nvidia stock slipped as financial media tied the session's losses to a broad selloff in chip and technology stocks rather than to any company-specific news. Regular-session close on Monday, November 2, 2026, 4:00 p.m. New York time. Stock prices: Yahoo Finance, cross-checked against the closing price on Nasdaq.com. Volume and 30-day average volume: Nasdaq.com. 52-week range: Yahoo Finance daily highs and lows since November 3, 2025. Indices and the 10-year Treasury yield: Yahoo Finance daily closes for the same date. Follow NVDA's latest price on our Nvidia (NVDA) stock price today page. Nvidia opened at $207.59, above Friday's close, and traded between $201.66 and $209.98 before ending the day just $0.40 above its low. Volume reached 119.3 million shares, 16.05% above the 102.8 million-share average, pointing to heavier trading than usual. The decline was close to the broader tech benchmark. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.07% to 25,164.36 and the S&P 500 slipped 0.51% to 7,541.40, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.41% to 51,983.98. Nvidia trailed the Nasdaq by 0.19 percentage points, and the US 10-year Treasury yield eased 3.5 basis points to 4.89%. Other chipmakers fell harder. AMD dropped 7.52%, Intel lost 8.80% and Marvell fell 12.72%, while Micron declined 5.78%, TSMC eased 1.85% and Broadcom slipped 1.18%. Nvidia closed 16.97% below its 52-week high and 23.00% above its 52-week low. None of the sources reviewed for this article reported Nvidia-specific news on Monday, and the drop tracked a wider selloff in chip and technology stocks. According to CNBC, the Nasdaq and S&P 500 fell after giving up early gains as investors continued to move out of tech stocks and continued to scrutinize names related to the AI buildout. Chipmakers took the heaviest hits. As reported by The Motley Fool, AMD shares, which fell nearly 11% on Friday, sold off further on Monday amid broader chip stock weakness, with no AMD-specific news. Per CNBC, Marvell fell after agreeing to buy Lumentum in a $115 billion deal, and Oracle declined after announcing a $10 billion stock offering and a $10 billion bond sale to fund its AI buildout. Nvidia's next earnings report, covering the fiscal 2027 third quarter that ended October 25, 2026, is due on Tuesday, November 17, with a conference call at 5 p.m. ET, according to the company's official announcement.
